summary: SIEM feed c030_link is degraded: 3.75% packet loss on the link between VF-1 port 1/5 and SIEM eth1 (32,625,000 sent vs 31,402,980 received), well above 0.1% threshold.

findings.root_cause: Physical/link-layer loss on the final hop between packet broker VF-1 port 1/5 and SIEM eth1: broker egressed 32,625,000 packets but SIEM eth1 captured only 31,402,980 (~1,222,020 packets / 3.75% lost). Most likely cause is faulty/dirty fibre/cable, bad optic/SFP, speed/duplex mismatch, or an unmonitored inline device dropping traffic after the broker.
findings.impact_on_tool: SIEM is missing ~3.75% of all forwarded traffic. Even though SIEM tolerates single-direction and truncated payload, this random loss creates blind spots for correlation, alerting and forensics - events and flows are incomplete.

recommended_fix.why: Loss is isolated to the cable/optic path after the broker egress counters, so fix Layer-1 first: check interface error counters, re-seat/clean/replace cable and SFPs, verify speed/duplex/autoneg on both ends, and bypass any unmonitored device between VF-1 and SIEM before changing broker policy.
